calibration_notes: Green class string (059, 065, 066, 068): the reviewers rated 059/065/068 Major and 066 Minor on identical evidence (same gold 'Green Account', same documents, same failing replay). Calibration's 'two document-supported readings' rule gives Major for all four; I upgraded 066. 068 is the strongest instance (the checking procedure's own example is 'Green Account (checking)') but stays Major because the gold spelling remains document-supported.

doc_004 'savings' vs gold 'business_savings' (056, 071): both Major and consistent. These are the only two tasks in the benchmark whose gold opens a business savings account, and the only four Green opens are 059/065/066/068, so no sibling outside this group carries either defect.
Post-clock gold values (072, 073, 074): all Major, consistent with calibration.

ATM rebate scope: 072 treats Bluest's rebate of Rho-Bank's own fee as well supported (note only), while 074 rates Purple's as a Major document_contradiction. The split is justified by the wording (Bluest: 'third-party ATM fees' / 'aggregate ATM fees'; Purple: 'refunds of ATM operator fees' and 'confirm that the charge was coded as an ATM operator fee'). But the 074 gold (broad Purple rebate) and the 075 gold (Purple's $2.50 not rebated) cannot both be right, so the gold set is inconsistent.

ATM fee stacking abroad: the 072-074 golds and seeded histories charge foreign withdrawals only the foreign fee (no out-of-network fee, e.g. Bluest Banamex 11/16 has no fee at all), while 075/076 need the out-of-network fee to stack. No personal-checking document states either rule (only the business Navy Blue doc says both apply). 075 and 076 are rated Major for it; in 072 (Light Green allowance count) and 074 (Light Blue allowance count, Purple foreign rows) the same ambiguity would change the nets under the stacking reading, but the agent sees the bank's non-stacking practice in the data, so I did not raise their severity. A fix should pick one rule and apply it to all five tasks.
Undefined closure 'Notice period' (060: 3 days, 062: 7 days) is treated as a note in both, which is consistent; if another group rated it as an issue, that is miscalibrated relative to these.
